config.descr_+: What the tools need to run the repo: repository, branches, paths, audit, lint and hooks.
config.descr_-: Not text for the docs (primary), not what gets built (data), not interruptores (`params.yaml`), not secrets (`.secrets/`).

primary.descr_+: What makes the docs: identity, texts, definitions, commands, features, log, index, modes and the schema of the memory itself.
primary.descr_-: Not paths or tool settings (config), not what gets built on disk (data), not hand-written code or modules.

docs.definition: Docs are all the markdown files about this project and how it operates. Every `.md` directly inside a folder of `config.paths.docs` is a doc, and every doc is generated from `data.content` by `pla-build`; a stray one fails the build.
docs.agent_note: note for the agent: this file is generated via the brain (memory.json) and binaries (build.rs)

intro: This repo is a public and living creature. Turn on your VPS or machine, connect your agents, code it, teach it something, and make a pull request on Github.
The servers will be 24/7 on. This is a personal project on autonomous coding and living information systems, but everyone is welcome in.
static_premises: Single source: `memory.json` is the brain, with exactly three primary keys (`config`, `primary`, `data`; see the table below), and `params.yaml` holds only the interruptores. Every `.md` in the repo root and in `agents/` is generated from them: edit only those two files and run `cargo run --release --bin pla-build` (see `agents/BUILD.md`). Modules in `agents/` subfolders are hand-written. Never edit generated files by hand.

Secrets: they live only in `.secrets/` at the repo root, which git ignores except its `.gitkeep`. Code and configs reference them by environment variable; their values never go into other files, the chat or external services.

Specific formats: markdown for information, json for the memory (`memory.json`), yaml for the interruptores (`params.yaml`), bash for system scripts (setup, links, servers) and Rust for everything else (see Premisas - dinámicas).
No duplication. Only one way of functional working, one memory file and one params file, symbolic links where matters, only one zettelkasten vault, etc.
Open source: everyone can collaborate with it (see `README.md` at the repo root for the contribution flow)

Pareto rule: 20% of the effort gives 80% of the result; when unsure, assume a similar split. Propose that 20% first, and more when it is for best practices. It also rules every description: `descr_+` (what a key is, the positive way) and `descr_-` (what it is not, the negative way) each say the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning.

Conservative, in general: prefer what exists and is known to work over what is new; change little at a time, keep every step reversible, and when in doubt ask instead of acting. The mode `ultra_conservative` makes this stricter when it is on.

Only small diff steps: this is not about git diffs but about knowledge. What the machine generates or learns on its own grows in small steps, and each step should ideally pass a verification process at several levels before it becomes part of the memory: consistent with what is already known, checked by machines (tests, linters, formal proofs) and reviewed by a human.
agents-md.brain_keys_intro: The memory (`memory.json`) has exactly three primary keys, each saying what it is (`descr_+`) and what it is not (`descr_-`):

dynamic_premises.brain: Brain: `memory.json` is the brain of plalast, the place everything is read from and written to. Everything in this file, and every other generated file (every `.md` in the root and in `agents/`, `.gitignore`, `.claude/settings.json`), is rebuilt from it byte by byte, with the interruptores of `params.yaml`.
dynamic_premises.write_order: Write order: delete > modify/edit > add. Before adding anything, first delete what is no longer needed, then modify or edit what exists, and add only what neither covers. This forces a kind of autonomous retraining of the memory, as long as the Pareto rule holds in each case.
dynamic_premises.problem_first: Problem-first: say, in plain human language, the problem that a tool or a set of tools solves, before naming any tool. Do not get carried away by proper names: names change, the problem stays. Follow "All models are wrong, but some are useful": every tool and every description is a model, judged by how useful it is and not by how true it is. This is the pragmatic philosophy the Pareto rule installs in our learning by reinforcement.
dynamic_premises.procedures: Procedures: short instructions in human language for recurring situations, in `agents/PROCEDURES.md` (from `primary.procedures`). Read the one that fits before acting.
dynamic_premises.intro: The current state of the repo: it changes as the repo grows, so check it against the repo when in doubt.
dynamic_premises.map: Map: `agents/structure.md` (where each path lives) and `cargo run --release --bin pla-recall -- [term]`.
dynamic_premises.modes_intro: Modes (`primary.mode`, each with its interruptor in `params.levers.mode`):

commands.tool_intro: Repo tool (details in `agents/BUILD.md`), from anywhere inside the repo:
code: Rust: `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo test <test_name>` (single test), `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
Verus: `cargo verus verify` (formal verification of the `verus!` code; install and usage in `agents/guides/verus.md`)
Lean 4: `lake build` (proofs of a Lean project; install and usage in `agents/guides/lean.md`)
Dafny: `dafny verify <file>.dfy` (verification of a Dafny file; install and usage in `agents/guides/dafny.md`)

tools_and_languages: Programs that must be fast, safe with memory and easy for an LLM to read and write, some of them proven correct: Rust, the default for every program and tool, with Verus for the proofs.
Proving that a statement is true, and keeping a growing base of checked facts: Lean 4.
Writing software together with the proof that it does what it says, in a form LLMs program well: Dafny, the default for LLM-programming.
candidates: Building web pages and user interfaces, and scripting or crawling the web: TypeScript.
good_practices: Interruptor: every document section and every mode has one in `params.levers` (also called a memory lever), with three values: `enabled` (always in the agent's memory), `on_demand` (its own file, read when needed; the default when none is set) or `disabled` (not built). Every new section or mode gets one when its default is not the right one.

File changes: when the user asks to touch any file, make the change in its section of `memory.json` (or `params.yaml` for interruptores) and rebuild with `pla-build` (the Rust build tool); never edit the output directly. Only the hand-written Rust code and the modules in `agents/` subfolders are edited in place.

Log: after every commit, merge or new branch, add an entry `{date, branch, commit, kind, descr}` to `primary.log` (a commit cannot hold its own hash, so it goes in the next commit) and rebuild; `agents/LOG.md` shows it.

Zettelkasten markdown spirit. A lot of things in the web are garbage, so notes in the agent-zettelkasten use CDU (Universal Decimal Classification) notation: the file name starts with the CDU code, then a kebab-case title, e.g. `004.8-llm-agents.md` (004.8 = artificial intelligence). The infrastructure will be up.
Lean memory: always-on docs hold only what an agent cannot learn by reading the repo; maps, overviews and reference material are `on_demand`.
Every rule earns its place: add one only when an agent repeats a mistake, and only if the agent could not find it in the repo; `pla-lint` keeps always-on docs under `config.lint.max_lines`.
Enforce, don't ask: rules that must never bend (never edit generated files, docs in sync with `memory.json`) are hooks or checks, not just instructions.
preferences: Naming: when the user says "la memoria", "el contexto" or "el json" (memory, context, the json), they mean `memory.json`.
Using languages LLM-friendly like Rust, Python or Go is desirable. Also, using LLM programming-specific languages is a tool to proceed with caution, but desirable at some point.
Formal verification is desirable, but very expensive. Watch out and connect to others' ideas instead of reinventing the wheel

commands.summary: regenerate docs, folders and links from `memory.json` and `params.yaml`
commands.detail: Builds the repo from `memory.json` and `params.yaml`. Idempotent: only writes what changed.

commands.summary: change nothing, fail if the repo drifted from the memory
commands.detail: Changes nothing; exits non-zero if the repo drifted from the memory (stale file, missing link, stray `.md`).

commands.summary: Claude Code hook: deny hand edits of generated files
commands.detail: Reads a Claude Code PreToolUse payload on stdin and denies Edit/Write on any file `pla-build` generates; `agents/hooks/protect-generated.sh` runs it.

commands.summary: print the repo map, or search it for `term`
commands.detail: Without `term`, prints the map: every path with its type and description, the module kinds, features, log, index, settings and levers. With `term`, searches all of it and the document text (case-insensitive), naming the file, section and lever of each hit.

commands.summary: check that the memory, the hand-written modules and the Rust code are well formed
commands.detail: Checks that `memory.json` and `params.yaml` are consistent and fully documented in `primary.schema`, that hand-written modules have the right shape (skill folders with `SKILL.md`, frontmatter `name` and `description`), that guides have their source, and that `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy` and, when Verus is installed, `cargo verus verify` pass. Pass `memory`, `modules` or `rust` to run only some areas.

commands.summary: look for secrets and personal data, vulnerable dependencies, broken links and branches out of sync
commands.detail: Looks for keys, tokens, emails and home-folder paths in what git would commit, files committed inside secret folders, known vulnerabilities in `Cargo.lock` (with `cargo-audit`), broken links, large files, uncommitted changes and branches out of sync. Pass `secrets`, `deps` or `repo` to run only some areas; `config.audit` holds its settings.

commands.summary: once per clone, so git's pre-commit hook refuses commits while `pla-build --check` fails
commands.detail: Run once per clone: git then uses `agents/hooks`, whose `pre-commit` refuses a commit while `pla-build --check` fails. `pla-audit` warns when it is not set.

commands.summary: once per machine, so `pla-audit deps` checks `Cargo.lock` against RustSec instead of skipping it
commands.detail: Run once per machine (it compiles from source and can take about 15 minutes): `pla-audit deps` then checks `Cargo.lock` against the RustSec advisory database. Without it, that check is skipped with a warning.

memory.json is the brain with config, primary and data (descr_+ / descr_-); params.yaml holds only the interruptores; Pareto a static premise; brain and write_order premises; mode ultra_conservative; rebuild test.

skills.definition: Skills: reusable procedures an agent loads when its description matches the task. One folder per skill with an uppercase SKILL.md whose frontmatter has `name` (the folder name, kebab-case) and `description`. Hand-written.

agents.definition: Subagents: one markdown file per subagent, whose body is its system prompt and whose frontmatter has `name` (the file name, kebab-case) and `description` (when to delegate to it). Hand-written.

rules.definition: Rules: modular instructions by topic, one non-empty markdown file each. Hand-written.

connectors.definition: Connectors: one MCP server per json file, in a neutral format: `name` (the file name), `transport` (`stdio` or `http`), `command` and `args` (stdio) or `url` (http), and `env`. Secrets are never written in them: `env` values are `${VAR}` references whose values live in `.secrets/`. Provider configs (such as Claude Code's `.mcp.json`) are not generated yet.

guides.definition: Guides: short how-tos for humans and agents about the tools of this project. Each is a hand-written markdown source; `pla-build` renders it to a PDF next to it.

agent_zettelkasten.definition: The single zettelkasten vault the agents use: CDU-named markdown notes outside this repo. Its path is `config.paths.modules.agent_zettelkasten`; the repo builds no link to it.

ultra_conservative.title: Mode ultra_conservative
ultra_conservative.when: the user turns it on, or a change is risky, irreversible or outward-facing
rules: Without the user's explicit confirmation: no commit, push, merge, branch deletion or file deletion.
Without the user's explicit confirmation: no change outside `memory.json` and `params.yaml`.
Keep every diff minimal, and say what would change before changing it.

procedures.definition: Procedures: mini-instructions of one or a few paragraphs, in human and not very concrete language, with no references to code or to the repo, readable by humans and machines alike. Each one has a `title` and `text` (a list of paragraphs).

solve-a-problem.title: Solving a problem
text: Start by saying the problem in plain words, as if to someone who knows none of the tools. If it cannot be said simply, it is not understood yet: keep asking until it can.
Then look for the smallest useful answer. Every answer is a model and every model is wrong somewhere; pick the one that is useful enough, try it, and keep it only while it keeps being useful.

change-something.title: Changing something
text: Before adding, look for what can be removed; before writing something new, look for what can be changed. Add only what neither covers.
Stop when the change gives most of its value. The last details cost the most and are worth the least; leave them for when they are needed.

describe-something.title: Describing something
text: Say what it is and what it is not, in a few words each. The two together draw its edge better than a long text on either side.
Keep only what carries most of the meaning. If a reader would lose nothing without a sentence, the sentence goes.

learn-from-a-mistake.title: Learning from a mistake
text: When the same mistake happens twice, write the smallest rule that would have prevented it, and put it where it will be read at the right moment.
Rules age. A rule that no longer prevents anything is noise: remove it, so the ones that matter stay visible.

act-under-doubt.title: Acting under doubt
text: When a step cannot be undone, or it reaches other people, ask first. When it can be undone, prefer doing it and showing the result over asking.
Say plainly what was done, what was not, and why. A clear partial result is more useful than an unclear complete one.

keys.config: What the tools need to run the repo: git, tool settings and every path. Its `descr_+` and `descr_-` say what it is and is not.
keys.config.descr_+: What `config` is (the positive way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
keys.config.descr_-: What `config` is not (the negative way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
keys.config.PLALAST_DIR: Where the repo lives: always `$PWD`, the repo root, which the tools find by walking up to `memory.json` and resolve at run time. No path is written, so the same value works on every machine and never leaks the user name.
keys.config.branches: `integration` (where work is committed) and `stable` (what receives merges); `pla-audit` checks they are in sync.
keys.config.audit: Settings of `pla-audit`: `allow` (exact strings or repo paths that are never reported, such as a public contact email) and `max_file_kb` (larger files are reported).
keys.config.lint: Settings of `pla-lint`: `always_on` (docs an agent loads every session) and `max_lines` (their combined line budget; over it, move sections to `on_demand`).
keys.config.hooks: Hooks that enforce the rules: `dir` (scripts; also git's `core.hooksPath`, so `pre-commit` runs `pla-build --check`) and `claude` (Claude Code hooks, rendered into `.claude/settings.json`; the PreToolUse hook denies hand edits of generated files).
keys.config.paths: Every path the tools use: `docs`, `on_demand` and `modules`.
keys.config.paths.docs: Folders whose `.md` files are docs (`.` is the repo root). Every `.md` directly inside them must be generated.
keys.config.paths.on_demand: Folder where `on_demand` sections are written as `<id>.md`.
keys.config.paths.modules: Per module kind (skills, agents, rules, connectors, guides): `dir` (where its modules are written) and `links` (provider -> folder that gets one symlink per module). Per external module of `primary.modules` (such as `agent_zettelkasten`): its path, relative to `modules/` (or to the folder of a structure symlink whose `target_ref` points at it). Keep it relative: an absolute path leaks your home folder. It depends on where the repo and the module sit on the machine, so a machine with another layout changes the value.
keys.params.levers: Interruptor (memory lever) of every document section, as `<doc>` -> `<section id>` -> value, and of every mode, as `mode` -> `<name>` -> value (see Memory levers). Unset means `on_demand`.
keys.primary: What makes the docs: project identity, texts, definitions, commands, features, log, index, modes and this schema. Its `descr_+` and `descr_-` say what it is and is not.
keys.primary.descr_+: What `primary` is (the positive way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
keys.primary.descr_-: What `primary` is not (the negative way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
keys.primary.project: Identity: `name`, `title` and `plalast_logo` (path of the project logo).
keys.primary.docs: Everything about the docs, the markdown files about this project and how it operates.
keys.primary.docs.definition: What counts as a doc, in words.
keys.primary.docs.agent_note: The note every generated doc carries on its second line, so an agent reading the file knows not to edit it by hand. Inserted by the `agent_note` block.
keys.primary.docs.on_demand: How `on_demand` sections are pointed at: the heading of the pointer list (`heading`) and the pointer line (`pointer`, with `{path}`, `{title}` and `{when}`). Their folder is `config.paths.on_demand`.
keys.primary.agents-md: The AGENTS.md text that no other key holds, split into fields; `data.content.agents_md` gives the doc its shape and points at them with `ref`.
keys.primary.agents-md.static_premises: Fixed premises: what the repo is, how it is built and the Pareto rule (the Premisas - estáticas section).
keys.primary.agents-md.brain_keys_intro: Intro of the table of primary keys (the `brain_keys` block) in the Premisas - estáticas section.
keys.primary.agents-md.dynamic_premises: Texts of the Premisas - dinámicas section (`brain`, `write_order`, `problem_first`, `procedures`, `intro`, `map`, `tools_intro`, `candidates_intro`, `modes_intro`); its lists are `commands`, `tools_and_languages`, `candidates` and the `modes` block.
keys.primary.agents-md.commands: Commands of the Premisas - dinámicas section: intros (`tool_intro`, `code_intro`) and the `code` commands; the tool commands come from `primary.commands`.
keys.primary.agents-md.candidates: Languages that may be used later.
keys.primary.agents-md.good_practices: How every agent works in the repo (the Buenas prácticas section).
keys.primary.agents-md.preferences: Preferences of the project owner (the Preferencias section).
keys.primary.features: Features of the project, as `feature_<n>` -> `{descr, status}` (both strings).
keys.primary.log: Project log: entries `{date, branch, commit, kind, descr}` in the order they happened; `kind` is `commit`, `merge` or `branch`. A commit cannot hold its own hash, so each one is logged in the next commit. LOG.md shows them newest first; `pla-audit` warns about commits missing from it.
keys.primary.index: Project index (empty for now; its format is not defined yet).
keys.primary.skills: Skills: `definition`; its folder and provider links are in `config.paths.modules`.
keys.primary.agents: Subagents: `definition`; its folder and provider links are in `config.paths.modules`.
keys.primary.rules: Rules: `definition`; its folder and provider links are in `config.paths.modules`.
keys.primary.connectors: MCP connectors: `definition`; its folder and provider links are in `config.paths.modules`. `pla-lint` checks each file's neutral format.
keys.primary.guides: Guides: `definition` and `render` (`pdf`: each .md is rendered to a .pdf by `pla-build`); folder and links in `config.paths.modules.guides`.
keys.primary.modules: External modules that live outside this repo, by name (such as `agent_zettelkasten`): each has a `definition` (what it is, in words); its path is `config.paths.modules.<name>`. A symlink in `modules/` is built only if `data.structure` has one for it.
keys.primary.mode: Modes, by name (such as `ultra_conservative`): `title`, `when` and `rules` (a list of strings). Its interruptor is `params.levers.mode.<name>`: `enabled` writes the rules into the `modes` block, `on_demand` writes them to `<config.paths.on_demand>/mode-<name>.md` and leaves a pointer, `disabled` drops them.
keys.primary.procedures: Procedures: `definition` and `items` (by id: `title` and `text`, a list of paragraphs in human language, with no backticks or file names; `pla-lint` checks it). Rendered into `agents/PROCEDURES.md` by the `procedures` block.
keys.primary.schema: This documentation of the memory and params format; `BUILD.md` renders its tables.
keys.primary.commands: The repo's commands, each `{cmd, summary, detail}`: AGENTS.md lists the summaries and BUILD.md the details.
keys.data: What gets built. Its `descr_+` and `descr_-` say what it is and is not.
keys.data.descr_+: What `data` is (the positive way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
keys.data.descr_-: What `data` is not (the negative way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
keys.data.structure: Every path, in order: `path`, `type`, `description`; optional `table` and `label` (its row in the Structure table), `gitkeep`, `secret`, `target`, `local` and `build`.
keys.data.content: One document per key: `head` (blocks before the first section), `sections` (`id`, `title`, `when`, `blocks`) and optional `agent_note: false` (no agent note, for adapter files such as `CLAUDE.md`, which is only `@AGENTS.md`). A `file` entry with `build: "<key>"` is rendered from it.

levers.enabled: Rendered inside its document as `## <title>`: always in the agent's memory.
levers.on_demand: Rendered to `<config.paths.on_demand>/<id>.md`; the document keeps only a pointer line under the on_demand heading, and the agent reads the file when `when` applies. The default when no value is set.

entry_types.dir: Creates the folder; `gitkeep: true` adds an empty `.gitkeep`; `secret: true` git-ignores its contents except `.gitkeep`. `path_ref` (a dotted path such as `config.paths.modules.skills.dir`) can replace `path`, and `label` may use `{path}`.
entry_types.symlink: Creates a link to `target`, relative to the link's folder; `target_ref` (a dotted config path such as `config.paths.modules.agent_zettelkasten`) can replace `target`. `local: true` marks a link that depends on the machine's layout: it is git-ignored, built only where its target exists, and removed where it does not.
entry_types.file + build: Renders `data.content.<build>`; `build: "gitignore"` renders `.gitignore` from the secret, ignored and local entries; `build: "claude_settings"` renders `.claude/settings.json` from `config.hooks.claude`.
entry_types.file + build: null: Hand-written code such as `Cargo.toml` or `src/`; never an `.md` in the root or `agents/`. Left as is.
entry_types.planned: Not created; listed as planned in the Structure table.

blocks.heading: `#` repeated `level` times, then `text`; `ref` (a dotted config path) can replace `text`
blocks.paragraph: `text` as is; `ref` (a dotted config path) can replace `text`
blocks.list: one `- item` line per item; `ref` (a dotted path to a list) can replace `items`, and `item` (a template such as `{cmd}: {summary}`) renders a list of objects
blocks.ordered_list: `1. item`, `2. item`, ...; `ref` (a dotted config path to a list of strings) can replace `items`
blocks.table: `header` and `rows` as a markdown table; or `ref` to a list of objects with `row` (one template per column) and optional `reverse`
blocks.structure_table: the Structure table, from the `data.structure` entries that have `table`
blocks.schema: a table of `primary.schema.<part>` with the given `header`
blocks.image: `![alt](src)`, or an HTML `` when `width` is set; `ref` (a dotted config path such as `primary.project.plalast_logo`) can replace `src`
blocks.agent_note: the text of `primary.docs.agent_note`, on the line right after the first one (no blank line); every doc has it as the second block of its `head`, unless the doc sets `agent_note: false`
blocks.modes: one `- Mode` line per mode of `primary.mode` that is not `disabled`: its rules when `enabled`, a pointer to `mode-<name>.md` when `on_demand`; nothing when every mode is disabled
blocks.brain_keys: a table `Key | Is (descr_+) | Is not (descr_-)` with one row per primary key of the memory (`config`, `primary`, `data`)
blocks.procedures: one `## <title>` per procedure of `primary.procedures.items`, followed by its paragraphs

data.descr_+: What gets built: every path of the repo (`structure`) and the shape of every generated doc (`content`).
data.descr_-: Not prose (texts live in primary and are pointed at with `ref`), not settings (config).

structure.table: The memory, the brain: `config`, `primary` and `data`; with the interruptores of `params.yaml`, every `.md` in the root and in `agents/` is generated from it (see `agents/BUILD.md`)
structure.description: The memory (config, primary, data). Hand-edited; with params.yaml, the only files that change for docs and structure.

head.text: Project rules and conventions for humans and agents: [agents/AGENTS.md](agents/AGENTS.md). Everything is generated from [memory.json](memory.json) and [params.yaml](params.yaml); see [agents/BUILD.md](agents/BUILD.md).

sections.title: Contributing
sections.when: preparing a branch or a pull request

items: Fork the repo and create a branch from `develop` (`feat/<topic>`, `fix/<topic>`, `docs/<topic>`).

Change only `memory.json` or `params.yaml` (or a hand-written module in an `agents/` subfolder), run `cargo run --release --bin pla-build`, and keep each change small: no duplication, Rust by default, markdown/json/yaml/bash formats.
Run `pla-lint` and `pla-audit` (see *Premisas - dinámicas* in agents/AGENTS.md): both must finish with no errors.
Open a pull request against `develop` describing what changed and why. `main` only receives merges from `develop`.

blocks.text: Run them from anywhere inside the repo: the tool walks up to the folder that holds `memory.json`. Symlinks need a Unix system (Linux or macOS). `pla-build` never replaces a real file or folder with a link, and never deletes anything except broken module links.

The brain is `memory.json`, with exactly three primary keys: `config` (what the tools need to run: git, settings, paths), `primary` (what makes the docs: identity, texts, definitions) and `data` (what gets built); each starts with `descr_+` and `descr_-`, what it is and is not. `params.yaml` has exactly `levers`, the interruptores. The tools join them as `config`, `primary`, `data` and `params`, so a dotted path such as `config.paths.modules.agent_zettelkasten` or `params.levers.agents_md.preferencias` works everywhere. Any other top-level key is an error.

sections.title: Memory levers: interruptores (params.yaml)
sections.when: changing what agents load into memory

blocks.text: Every section of every document has an interruptor in `params.levers.<doc>.<section id>`, and every mode of `primary.mode` one in `params.levers.mode.<name>`. An unset one is `on_demand`; a lever for a section or mode that does not exist, or a value outside this table, stops the build.
Switching a section from `on_demand` to `disabled` leaves its old file behind: `pla-build` reports it as a stray `.md` and fails until you delete it.

sections.title: Structure entry types
sections.when: adding or changing a path in data.structure

blocks.text: Each section is rendered as `## <title>` followed by its blocks. Blocks are separated by one blank line, except `agent_note`, which goes right under the first line; every file ends with one newline.

sections.title: Adding a module
sections.when: adding a skill, subagent or rule

blocks.text: Write the module in its folder (for example `agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) and run `pla-build`: each provider in `config.paths.modules.<kind>.links` gets one link for it (`.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../agents/skills/<name>`), never a whole folder. Links of deleted modules are removed on the next build.

Guides are modules too: write `agents/guides/<name>.md` and run `pla-build`, which renders `agents/guides/<name>.pdf` from it (headings, paragraphs, lists and code blocks; inline markup is flattened). The PDF is deterministic, so `pla-build --check` reports a stale one.

Deleting an entry from `memory.json` does not delete it from disk. `pla-build --check` reports leftover `.md` files in the root and `agents/`; delete them once you have confirmed they are no longer needed.
